# Assembling your Elements 

You will ensure that your data and plotting scripts needed for creating your plot are used to build the up-to-date version of the plot.

## Code Block for Sourcing Your Scripts

```{r}
# source data-related scripts 
cleaned_rankings_data <- readRDS(file = here::here("data","processed","cleaned_rankings_data.rds")) 
head(cleaned_rankings_data)

atp_singles_data <- readRDS(file = here::here("data","processed","atp_singles.Rds")) 
head(atp_singles_data)

# source plotting script(s)
save_plot_png <- function(
    plot,
    file_name, 
    figs_dir,
    units = "px",
    width = 1600,
    height = 1100,
    dpi = 300) {
  
  file_path <- here::here(figs_dir, file_name)
  
  ggsave(
    filename = file_path,
    plot = plot,
    device = "png",
    units = units,
    width = width,
    height = height,
    dpi = dpi
  )
}
```

## The Modified Plot

Describe why you might want to implement this approach.

I wanted to implement more detail in the legend of my other plot, being that I adjusted it to have winnning percentage instead of total wins, and the other plot I had included very little description of what was going on in the plot. The newer plot is more complex due to a percantage, and I wanted to use some of the functions learned in class.


## Code Block for Embedding your PNG

```{r}
# plot with a caption

#| fig.cap: "This plot visualizes winning percentages of our five focus players on specific surfaces."
#| fig.align: "center" # to center plot on page if desired
#| out.width: "100%"   # or some other % appropriate for you site

knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figs", "majorsviz.png"))
```
